lesson.title: The Winner Can Be the Wrong Shot
lesson.hook: A low-percentage winner teaches you to repeat the choice that will usually cost you.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time a risky winner lands, ask whether you would choose it ten times.

pro.label: Ferrero on Alcaraz, 2025
pro.moment: Juan Carlos Ferrero, then his coach: "He knows that he has to work on his consistency. I've told him so many times and that's what we're doing."
pro.read: Applause judges the outcome. Champions judge the choice.

drill.name: The ten-ball test
drill.how: Pick a target and hit 10 balls at it from the same feed. Fewer than 7 in? It's too ambitious for a match. Move it a metre inside the line and go again.

lesson.cue: Would I choose it ten times?

steps.name: The line winner
steps.sit: Off a low, neutral ball, you go down the line and clip the paint. Winner.
steps.q: What does that one winner tell you?
opts: The line was the only shot
That it went in — this time
steps.payoff: One winner only proves that one ball went in.
steps.principle: Judge the choice by what you knew before you hit it, not by where it landed.
steps.why: Clipping the line feels like proof. It isn't: from this ball the same shot misses often, and the ten tries show it.
steps.take: Would you choose it ten times? Judge the choice, not the applause.

lines.A: One winner can't show the margin — here are ten tries of the same shot.
lines.B: Nothing forced the line — the big crosscourt was there too.
lines.C: Right — this one landed. Ten tries show how often it would.
lines.D: A low ball rarely earns full pace — look at the misses.

steps.name: Same ball, ten tries
steps.sit: Same ball again. Choose before you see where it lands.
steps.q: Which shot would you pick ten times?
steps.payoff: The bigger target leaves room for the small misses everyone makes.
steps.principle: Pick the shot that still works when you hit it slightly wrong.
steps.why: From the same ball, the crosscourt window gives you more net and more court with the same balance. Ten tries show what one winner hides.
steps.take: Same ball: pick the target that lands ten times out of ten.

lines.A: The big crosscourt window lands every time — rally on.
lines.B: Flat from a low ball — into the net too often.
lines.C: The line again — it misses almost as often as it wins.
lines.D: It lands, but short and slow — they get there and punish it.

steps.name: The high short ball
steps.sit: Now the ball is high and short. You're set, and they're pulled wide.
opts: Open court, right on the line
steps.payoff: This time the risk was earned before you hit it.
steps.principle: Risk is right when the ball, your balance and the space all support it.
steps.why: High contact, set feet and open court change the odds. The score can't make those things true.
steps.take: High, set, open court: attack — with margin.

lines.A: Safe, but you'd earned more — chance missed.
lines.B: Hard at them — they're on it and pass you.
lines.C: Open court, well inside the lines — they can't get there.
lines.D: Right on the line — too many land wide.
